questions.explain: A daily score snapshotted from catalog views with change detection catches misconfiguration (new sysadmin, re-enabled xp_cmdshell) within 24 hours and names exactly what moved — versus quarterly audits that find it eventually.
options: It eliminates the need for any access reviews
It satisfies compliance with less documentation
It converts quarterly audit findings into 24-hour detection that names exactly what changed
It automatically fixes every misconfiguration it finds
questions.q: Why does the chapter recommend scoring the attack surface daily instead of quarterly?

questions.explain: A global model flags every service account daily for merely differing from humans; a per-login baseline learns each principal's own normal pattern (e.g., the ETL account's 3 databases at 01:00–03:00) and flags genuine deviations.
options: Global models train faster on smaller datasets
Per-login baselines learn each principal's own normal behavior, so deviations are meaningful instead of flagging every service account daily
Per-login models require no feature engineering
Global models cannot use Isolation Forest
questions.q: Why are behavioral anomaly models built per login rather than as one global model?

questions.explain: The top_deviating_features column names which dimensions deviated most (e.g., 'tables_read, distinct_hosts'), telling the responder where to look in seconds instead of dumping a raw score.
options: It reduces the model's memory footprint
It satisfies a regulatory reporting format
It speeds up model training
It names the most-deviated dimensions so responders know where to look immediately
questions.q: What makes the anomaly alert actionable in the chapter's design?

questions.explain: Joining permission snapshots against actual usage (SQL Audit/Query Store) identifies principals holding powerful grants on objects untouched for 180+ days — revocation candidates with near-zero risk and evidence attached.
options: Join permission snapshots against actual usage to find powerful grants on long-untouched objects — near-zero-risk revocation candidates
Revoke all permissions older than 30 days automatically
Grant every principal db_owner so reviews are unnecessary
Delete the permission history table monthly to save space
questions.q: How does the chapter recommend identifying safe privilege-revocation candidates?

questions.explain: Security remediation keeps humans on approval: allowlisted reversible actions (DISABLE LOGIN, never DROP), mandatory blast radius and rollback per step, AUDIT_ONLY default for medium/low — the LLM drafts, the human approves.
options: The LLM executes remediation autonomously for speed
The LLM drafts the plan with allowlisted reversible actions, blast radius, and rollback per step — a human approves before anything executes
All findings are auto-remediated with DROP LOGIN
Remediation plans are generated but never executed, for audit purposes only
questions.q: What is the chapter's stance on autonomous security remediation?
